title_en: Capital Group’s Wilson on Finding Coiled Springs
title_zh: 资本集团威尔逊谈寻找蓄势待发的“弹簧”股
subtitle_zh: 资本集团成长ETF（CGGR）首席投资官艾伦·威尔逊谈成长投资、估值、护城河与多经理体系
summary_zh: 本期 Inside Active 由 Bloomberg Intelligence 的 David Cohne 主持，对话 Capital Group 投资组合经理、Capital Group Growth ETF（代码 CGGR）首席投资官 Alan Wilson，探讨成长投资的宽口径理解与 Capital Group 的多经理体系。Wilson 强调成长不应只等同于漂亮的营收（top line）增长：一只被彻底抛弃的周期股从低点反弹到周期顶部同样能带来大量资本增值，因此组合里既有传统成长股，也有像压紧的弹簧（coiled springs）般等待周期反转、普通成长指数不会持有的标的——关键是一家公司的增长引擎跑道要长到足以赚回买入价。他用雨伞与太阳镜的寓言说明自己方法的核心：模糊地判断三年后世界的样子，投资就会变容易。CGGR 采用 Capital Group 标志性的多经理体系，由约七位方法互补、各自能在完整周期跑赢的经理人从同一个农贸市场（大型投资会议）采购想法，首席投资官负责协调互补技能并对市值等规则达成一致；Wilson 的薪酬按一至八年混合业绩考核，鼓励长期视野。节目还谈到护城河（moats）、仓位大小取决于对未来图景的契合度、价格、持久性与若判断错误能否出得去，医疗占比约四分之一，以及当下他最关注的机会——AI 与发电需求对实体基础设施（石油、电力）的约束，可能孕育下一批压紧的弹簧。
description: Capital Group’s Wilson on Finding Coiled Springs

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond soundbites and headlines and looks deeper into their processes, challenges, and philosophies in security selection. I'm David Cohn. I lead mutual fund and active research at Bloomberg Intelligence. Growth investing can sound relatively straightforward. Find companies that grow faster than the market and hold them as that growth compounds over time. But identifying durable growth is much harder in practice. Investors have to determine how long a company can sustain its growth how much of that opportunity is already reflected in its valuation, and what could cause the investment thesis to change. And that opportunity set doesn't necessarily have to be limited to the companies or sectors traditionally associated with growth. A flexible approach can look across industries and different types of businesses for companies with the potential to create value over the long term. So today, I wanted to explore how that works in practice, how growth opportunities are identified in research, how valuation and risk factor into security selection, how a portfolio is constructed around those ideas, and how Capital Group's multi-manager approach influences the process. Joining me to discuss that is Alan Wilson, a portfolio manager at Capital Group and principal investment officer of the Capital Group Growth ETF, ticker CGGR. Alan, thanks for joining me.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听《Inside Active》（深入主动管理），这是一档关于主动管理型基金经理的播客，我们不满足于金句和头条，而是更深入地探究他们在选股上的流程、挑战与理念。我是大卫·科恩（David Cohne），负责彭博行业研究（Bloomberg Intelligence）的共同基金与主动管理研究。成长型投资听起来相对简单：找到那些增长快于市场的公司，然后长期持有，让增长随时间不断复利累积。但在实践中，识别出可持续的增长要难得多。投资者必须判断一家公司能把增长维持多久、这一机会有多少已经反映在其估值之中，以及什么因素可能导致投资逻辑发生改变。而且，这个机会集并不一定局限于传统上与“成长”挂钩的那些公司或行业。一种灵活的方法可以横跨不同行业和不同类型的企业，去寻找那些有潜力在长期创造价值的公司。所以今天，我想探讨这在实践中是如何运作的：如何在研究中发现成长机会，估值和风险如何纳入选股考量，如何围绕这些思路构建投资组合，以及资本集团（Capital Group）的多经理体系如何影响这一过程。今天和我一起讨论的嘉宾是艾伦·威尔逊（Alan Wilson），他是资本集团的投资组合经理，也是资本集团成长ETF（代码CGGR）的首席投资官。艾伦，感谢你的到来。

turns.en: Thanks for having me, Dave.
turns.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，戴夫。

turns.en: So, Alan, when we think about, or when you think about growth investing, what does growth actually mean to you? You know, what characteristics tell you a company has the potential to compound value over a long period of time?
turns.zh: 那么，艾伦，当我们——或者说当你——思考成长型投资时，“成长”对你来说究竟意味着什么？有哪些特征能告诉你，一家公司有潜力在很长一段时间里让价值不断复利累积？

turns.en: So, first of all, you know, at Capital, one of the ways that I was always trained to think about this is that we're looking at growth of capital, growth of the investment, which many people often associate with. just great top line. But in fact, if you have a cyclical that's rebounding from washed out completely to being really enthusiastically looked at at the top of the cycle, you can get a lot of growth in capital. And I think if you look at our portfolio, one of the things you will see is a mixture of companies that have traditional growth characteristics from a top line perspective, but also there are these coiled springs waiting for a cycle to turn. And that's one of the things that's typically not in a typical growth index. But If to your question about one of the things, what are the things that you look for? Look, what you want is the company's current engine to have a long enough runway that it will pay for the price of getting in to own the company, right? And that depends on the industry. It depends on the opportunity. Sometimes you see long runways. Sometimes they're relatively short. But constructing a portfolio that's a balance of all those is what our system has really decided to do.
turns.zh: 首先，你要知道，在资本集团，我一直被训练用这样一种方式来思考：我们关注的是资本的增长、投资本身的增长，而很多人往往把这仅仅跟漂亮的营收（top line）挂钩。但实际上，如果你持有一只周期股，它从被彻底抛弃的低点反弹、到在周期顶部被市场热情追捧，你同样能获得大量的资本增值。我想如果你看看我们的投资组合，你会发现其中一类公司具有传统的成长特征（从营收角度看），但同时也有那些像压紧的弹簧一样、等待周期反转的公司。而后者通常是普通成长指数里不会有的东西。回到你的问题——你会寻找哪些东西？是这样的：你想要的，是一家公司当前的“增长引擎”拥有足够长的跑道，长到能够赚回你买入并持有这家公司所付出的价格，对吧？这取决于行业，取决于具体机会。有时你会看到很长的跑道，有时则相对较短。而构建一个在所有这些之间取得平衡的投资组合，正是我们的体系真正致力于去做的事。

turns.en: Okay. And so, you know, CGGR is, you know, it pursues growth as an objective rather than, you know, adhering to a particular growth style, kind of as you mentioned. How does that distinction change the universe of companies you're willing to look at?
turns.zh: 好的。CGGR追求的是把“成长”当作一个目标，而不是——就像你提到的——拘泥于某种特定的成长风格。这种区别如何改变你愿意去审视的公司范围？

turns.en: So we look at everything. In fact, if you think about our investment process, we have a large general meeting or several large ones where we discuss all types of ideas. And you come away from that and put things in a different portfolio. So it almost is, imagine a bunch of restaurants that are going to a central restaurant. farmer's market to get ingredients. So it's not like we have, oh, we're going to have a growth meeting and just talk about those ideas. And so one of the things that happens is that you may hear an idea that traditionally one might not associate. It might be a cyclical, as I said, that's super depressed. You go, oh my God, I can see a double in this stock whenever the cycle turns. We tend to have a long horizon. In fact, I've compensated on a blend of my one year to eight year results. And so you can say, look, over an extended period of time, this cycle will turn when this happens. In fact, one of the places you can look at this now is housing, for example. Obviously, the housing market isn't robust, but I would be really surprised if over the course of my four-year visibility lens that you don't have a return. And then so my question is, do I have a company that can double that? And so that's where the idea of sourcing tends to come from and how they tend to come.
turns.zh: 我们什么都看。事实上，如果你想想我们的投资流程，我们会召开一场（或几场）大型会议，在会上讨论各种类型的投资想法。你从会议中带走一些想法，放进不同的投资组合里。所以这几乎可以想象成——一群餐厅都去同一个中心化的农贸市场采购食材。并不是说，哦，我们要开一个“成长会议”、只讨论那些成长类的想法。因此会发生这样一种情况：你可能会听到一个传统上人们不会归为“成长”的想法。它可能像我说的，是一只被极度压抑的周期股。你会想，天哪，一旦周期反转，我能看到这只股票翻倍。我们的视野往往很长。事实上，我的薪酬是基于我一年到八年业绩的一个混合来评定的。所以你可以说，看，在一段较长的时间里，这个周期会反转、会是这样。事实上，你现在可以关注的一个领域就是房地产（housing）。显然，房地产市场目前并不强劲，但如果在未来四年的可见度范围内它都不出现复苏，那我会非常惊讶。那么我的问题就是：我手上有没有一家能借此翻倍的公司？这就是这些投资思路的来源，也是它们往往如何被——

turns.en: Into the portfolio.
turns.zh: ——纳入投资组合。

turns.en: The other thing, and then I'll be quiet for a second, The other thing that's interesting about the way we manage our portfolio is that there are several managers on this fund. It's the capital system, I think, as most of your listeners are probably familiar with. But if you have a bunch of complementary portfolio managers in terms of approach and a style of what appeals, and they all outperform over a cycle, the question is some might be hot or cold at different times. What you will tend to find is a spread of ideas that wind up in the portfolio as listing through the areas makes it feel attractive.
turns.zh: 另外一点——然后我就先安静一会儿——我们管理组合的方式还有一点很有意思：这只基金有好几位经理。这就是资本集团的体系，我想你的大多数听众可能都熟悉。但如果你有一群在方法和风格上互补、各自都有吸引力的投资组合经理，而且他们在一个完整周期里都能跑赢大盘，那么问题就是——他们中有些人在不同时候可能状态火热或低迷。你会发现，最终进入组合的是一批分散多样的想法，因为在各个领域里逐一梳理，会让组合显得颇具吸引力。

turns.en: Okay. And so you mentioned you're looking at, what, eight to 10 years? I think that's what you said.
turns.zh: 好的。你提到你在看……八到十年？我记得你是这么说的。

turns.en: Well, I said my compensation window is one, three, five, and eight. There's probably more data than people want to have. But basically, it's the organization's inclination to try to have me to look out beyond just what's in the market today.
turns.zh: 嗯，我说的是我的薪酬考核窗口是一年、三年、五年和八年。这里的数据可能比人们想知道的还要多。但基本上，这体现了公司的一种倾向：让我把眼光放得比“当下市场里有什么”更长远一些。

turns.en: Okay. So then what would give you the confidence that a growth you're seeing at a company is durable rather than just temporary? Or is it kind of with the different managers that kind of get spread out, you know, that risk?
turns.zh: 好的。那么，是什么让你有信心认为，你在一家公司身上看到的成长是可持续的，而非仅仅是暂时的？还是说，靠不同的经理在某种程度上分散了这种风险？

turns.en: You know, it depends on the industry, right? There are some things. So for example, if you think about one of the things that can be so attractive about the medical and pharmaceutical area in particular, is that if you wind up solving a real problem and you have the patent protection, you can actually see quite a long runway for those types of solutions. Now, as people start to come to a cliff, right, as that starts to run out, that's when this, when this, uh, when the stocks tend to often weaken unless there's something as a follow-on behind it.
turns.zh: 你知道，这取决于行业，对吧？有些领域是这样的。举个例子，医疗和制药领域之所以常常如此有吸引力，一个原因就是：如果你最终解决了一个真实存在的问题，并且拥有专利保护，那么这类解决方案其实能看到相当长的跑道。而当人们开始接近“专利悬崖”、也就是保护期开始耗尽时，这些股票往往会走弱——除非其背后还有后续产品（follow-on）接棒。

turns.en: But for example, about.
turns.zh: 但比如说，关于……

turns.en: Almost a quarter of my portfolio right now is in healthcare, drug-related types of stocks. We can come back later if you want as to why those might be particularly appealing. But that has a very different one way than something that may be more fashion-oriented, right? If you think about a company right now like Nike, that's largely a fashion business. And But that's also one that's extremely depressed right now. So that might be one of those coiled springs, but you just want that spring to pop up. That is not necessarily a buy it, hold it, set it, and forget it. So it really is very much business dependent.
turns.zh: 我目前组合中差不多有四分之一投在医疗、药物相关的股票上。如果你愿意，我们稍后可以回头谈谈为什么这些标的可能特别有吸引力。但这一领域的“跑道”，与那些更偏时尚导向的东西非常不同，对吧？如果你想想现在像耐克（Nike）这样的公司，它在很大程度上是一门时尚生意。但它现在也被压得极低。所以它可能是那种“压紧的弹簧”之一，你就是等着这根弹簧弹起来。这并不一定是那种“买入、持有、一劳永逸”的标的。所以这真的非常依赖于具体的生意。

turns.en: Okay. Yeah, one of the things with growth investing, I think a lot of folks are wondering just, you know, after what's been happening the last couple of years is just, you know, do valuations still count right now? And so I'm just curious. How does, you know, how important is valuation in your process? You know, what gives you kind of confidence you're not paying too much for a great business?
turns.zh: 好的。是的，说到成长型投资，我想很多人都在琢磨——尤其是在过去几年发生的事情之后——估值现在到底还重要吗？所以我很好奇：在你的流程中，估值有多重要？是什么让你有信心，自己没有为一家优秀的公司付出过高的价格？

turns.en: Dave, valuation always counts, right?
turns.zh: 戴夫，估值永远重要，对吧？

turns.en: It always does, right?
turns.zh: 它一直都重要，对吧？

turns.en: Look, there's some things that are so extraordinary that it's worth paying up for, but valuation always matters, right? You can pay too much for something extraordinary and you can, and there's also kind of a price at which everything is attractive. And so part of the judgment of portfolio construction and why it's great to have several different ears listening is that people can hear that equation and find value in very different places. I see the other thing that's really kind of interesting is to watch. I actually don't watch the index that much, but it's interesting to me periodically where I will watch stocks that go into and out of the various indices, right? So right now, caterpillars are quote-unquote growth stock, right? And the energy stocks are becoming quote-unquote growth stocks. Those were coil springs previously, right? They weren't considered growth that then did well as the cycle turned. And then, you know, they came into the indices.
turns.zh: 你看，有些东西极其出色，为它多付点钱是值得的，但估值永远重要，对吧？你为一件卓越的东西也可能付出过高的价格；同时，也总存在一个价格，在那个价位上一切都变得有吸引力。所以，组合构建中判断力的一部分——以及为什么有好几双不同的耳朵在倾听是件好事——就在于，人们能听懂这个等式，并在非常不同的地方发现价值。我觉得另一件很有意思、值得观察的事情是——我其实并不太关注指数本身，但我时不时会去留意那些被纳入或被剔除出各个指数的股票，这很有意思，对吧？比如说现在，卡特彼勒（Caterpillar）算是所谓的“成长股”了，对吧？能源股也正在变成所谓的“成长股”。它们此前是“压紧的弹簧”，对吧？它们并不被认为是成长股，随后随着周期反转而表现良好，然后才被纳入指数。

turns.en: There's a debate.
turns.zh: 这方面是有争议的。

turns.en: I think sometimes, in fact, the indices tend to bring those types of stocks in exactly when it's maturing. But, you know, that's an opportunity for an active manager if you're.
turns.zh: 我觉得有时候，事实上，指数往往恰恰在这类股票已经成熟的时候才把它们纳入进来。但你知道，对主动管理者来说，这就是一个机会，只要你——

turns.en: Right on it. Yeah, definitely. So could you walk us through your... You know, your investment process, you know, walk me through how an idea typically enters your portfolio, where the research begins and, you know, what needs to happen before an interesting company becomes an actual investment in the portfolio. Sure. Okay.
turns.zh: ——紧紧跟上（right on it）。是的，绝对如此。那么，你能不能带我们走一遍你的……你的投资流程？给我讲讲一个想法通常是如何进入你的组合的，研究从哪里开始，以及在一家有意思的公司真正成为组合里的一项投资之前，需要发生些什么。当然。好的。

turns.en: And then just to set the context for your listeners out there, you know, I've been at Capital for over 30 years. Our average analyst, I think the tenure is something like 12 or 13. The typical PM tenure is, you know, in the high teams numbers. And so I say that because what you're having at these investment calls is a group of people who have worked together for at least a decade, over a decade, and we're getting together and just talking about what people have seen in the world. So that's that farmer's market I described of ideas that one is approaching. My own personal approach is that I think that if you can figure out what the world's going to look like, even in a hazy way, about three years out, investing becomes easy. A parable I tell all the time, there are only two stocks, one sold umbrellas and one sold sunglasses. And I told you it was going to rain for the next three years. I don't think you'd have any question as to which stock you wanted to hold. Conversely, if I told you that we're going to go into the world's worst drought, it's very clear to People don't typically know what the weather is, so they diversify and buy a little bit of each. I think with talented analysts, with a lot of context and conviction, and some other perspective, that you can kind of get some hazy views of what the world looks like. So I tend to walk in with sort of this, what do I think the world looks like? And then I'm listening for ideas that fit into that type of world. And that's the pathway for those to come into the portfolio.
turns.zh: 我先为你的听众交代一下背景。我在资本集团已经工作超过30年了。我们分析师的平均任期，我想大概是12、13年左右。而典型的投资组合经理任期，则接近二十年（十七八年）。我之所以这么说，是因为你在这些投资电话会上面对的，是一群已经共事至少十年、甚至超过十年的人，我们聚在一起，就是聊聊各自在世界上看到了什么。这就是我描述的那个“农贸市场”——一个人带着想法去那里采购。我个人的方法是：我认为，如果你能弄清楚——哪怕只是模模糊糊地——大约三年后世界会是什么样子，投资就会变得容易。我经常讲一个寓言：世上只有两只股票，一只卖雨伞，一只卖太阳镜。如果我告诉你未来三年会一直下雨，我想你不会有任何疑问该持有哪只股票。反过来，如果我告诉你我们将迎来世界上最严重的干旱，那也很清楚。可人们通常不知道“天气”会怎样，所以他们会分散投资，两种都买一点。我认为，凭借有才华的分析师、大量的背景信息和信念，再加上其他一些视角，你多少能获得一些关于“世界会是什么样”的模糊判断。所以我往往会带着这样一种视角走进去：我认为世界会是什么样子？然后我去倾听那些契合这种未来世界的想法。这就是这些想法进入组合的路径。

turns.en: I'll hear them.
turns.zh: 我会去倾听这些想法。

turns.en: I'll talk with the analyst. I'll talk with my other portfolio managers. I may well have visited them right at this point. Often it's sort of stocks that I've known for a while that have sort of come back into orbit, like comets coming by periodically as opposed to a brand new idea. But that's at least my own particular pathway. It is not especially. valuation sensitive. It's more, does the idea fit what I think the near future is going to look like?
turns.zh: 我会和分析师交流，也会和其他投资组合经理交流。到了这个阶段，我可能已经去实地拜访过这些公司了。这些往往是我已经关注了一段时间、又重新回到我“轨道”里的股票，就像彗星周期性地掠过，而不是全新的想法。但这至少是我个人特有的路径。它对估值并不是特别敏感。更多的是一种判断：这个想法是否契合我认为的“近期未来的样子”？

turns.en: Is there anything that you spend a lot of time on, you know, trying to understand a company you think the market either misunderstands or isn't really looking far enough to appreciate?
turns.zh: 有没有什么是你花大量时间去钻研的——你试图去理解一家你认为市场要么误解了、要么没有看得足够长远因而未能欣赏其价值的公司？

turns.en: You know.
turns.zh: 你知道……

turns.en: Sure.
turns.zh: 当然。

turns.en: But the thing is, it's different for each company, right? Like everyone wants some master key. So if you just look at this thing over here, it will always tell you the thing to look at. But for each company, which is, by the way, it's what makes the job interesting. It's what makes it compelling for me still after 35 years is because each question for each company is a different one. And then whether people can execute on it is a different one. And on top of all that, when you combine those difficulties, You know, God, if I'm great at this, I'm right three times out of five, you know? So it's just interesting enough to get someone to be, to kind of be that perpetual puzzle that is always interesting and never perfectly solved.
turns.zh: 但问题是，每家公司都不一样，对吧？人人都想要一把万能钥匙：好像你只要盯着这边的某个东西看，它就总能告诉你该看什么。但对每家公司来说——顺便说一句，这正是这份工作有意思的地方，也是让我在干了35年之后仍然觉得它有吸引力的原因——因为每家公司要回答的问题都各不相同，而这家公司能否执行到位，又是一个各不相同的问题。更重要的是，当你把这些难点叠加起来……天哪，就算我在这方面很在行，我五次里也就对三次，你懂吧？所以它刚好有意思到足以让人成为——成为那个永远有趣、却永远无法被完美解开的谜题。

turns.en: Okay. What about management teams? You know, how important is that assessment? You know, is there something that tells you, you know, this could be agnostic to different companies or sectors, you know, or industries. Is there anything that tells you a management team can successfully reinvest capital and extend the company's growth opportunity?
turns.zh: 好的。那管理团队呢？这项评估有多重要？有没有什么信号能告诉你——这一点可能对不同公司、不同行业或板块都是通用的——有没有什么能让你判断，一个管理团队能够成功地再投资资本、并延展公司的成长机会？

turns.en: Look, it's very business dependent, right? If you've got a business that involves taking $ 10 bills and sticking them in a shredder, I don't know what the, I don't even know if I can find a management team that's going to be, you know, that can market the resulting paper good enough. Conversely, you know, there's some businesses that are so extraordinary.
turns.zh: 你看，这非常依赖于具体的生意，对吧？如果你手上有一门生意，本质上是把10美元的钞票塞进碎纸机里，那我都不知道——我甚至不确定我能不能找到一个管理团队，能把碎出来的纸屑营销得足够好。反过来，也有些生意本身就极其出色。

turns.en: What is it?
turns.zh: 是什么呢？

turns.en: I think, I think Buffett was famous for, you want a business so good even an idiot could run it, but sooner or later one will, right? I mean, in fact, often some of my more interesting ideas are businesses that are doing well kind of in spite of themselves. That shows me the strength of the business, right? But the key really is, though, that you have the right manager's ethos, et cetera, with.
turns.zh: 我想，我记得巴菲特有句名言：你想要一门好到连傻子都能经营的生意，因为迟早会有一个傻子来经营它，对吧？我是说，事实上，我一些更有意思的想法，恰恰是那些几乎“不顾自身”（in spite of themselves）都能表现良好的生意。这向我展示了这门生意本身的实力，对吧？但真正的关键在于，你要有正确的管理者气质、理念等等，同时搭配——

turns.en: The right industry. Sure, just in terms of, You know, when we think of growth, you know, some companies benefit from certain cycles, you know, versus other companies that see, you know, likely see growth over a longer term, you know, strong growth. Is there anything that, you know, separates those companies that see the longer term growth versus, you know, maybe a company that's just benefiting during different specific cycles?
turns.zh: ——正确的行业。当然。那么，就……你知道，当我们想到“成长”时，有些公司受益于某些周期，而另一些公司则可能在更长的时间里实现增长——强劲的增长。有没有什么能把那些实现长期增长的公司，与那些也许只是在特定周期中受益的公司区分开来？

turns.en: Look, a lot of it is just the environment. I think if, you know, what's interesting for listeners, just take NVIDIA, right? Everybody talks about, go back and look at NVIDIA's chart over time. Literally, what they've done is they've had these processors that are really good at doing multiple things at once. They did them for graphics. But there have been these different waves where the desire for those products, whether it's, oh my God, we're going to run really nice graphics on a computer, or oh my God, we're going to use this stuff to really solve cryptographic problems. So, oh my God, we're going to use this stuff to large language. But each time you saw this gigantic wave of people enthusiastically adopting that would crest and roll over.
turns.zh: 你看，这在很大程度上取决于所处的大环境。我想，对听众来说有意思的是——就拿英伟达（NVIDIA）来说，对吧？大家都在说，回头去看看英伟达这些年的股价走势图。它们真正做到的，是造出了这些非常擅长“同时处理多件事情”的处理器。它们最初是为图形（graphics）而做的。但随后出现了一波又一波不同的浪潮，人们对这些产品的需求——无论是“天哪，我们要在电脑上运行非常漂亮的图形画面”，还是“天哪，我们要用这些东西去真正解决密码学问题”，再到“天哪，我们要用它来做大语言模型”。但每一次，你都会看到一波巨大的人群热情地涌入采用，然后到达顶点、再翻滚回落。

turns.en: And so you would have these giant spikes.
turns.zh: 于是你会看到这些巨大的尖峰。

turns.en: And people would debate when it was on the other side of those spikes whether NVIDIA was no longer a growth company. So really, in any business, it's just kind of the duration of what it is that you're providing. And by the way, no one has permanent duration, I guess is what I'm saying. So it's one of the reasons that I really think that it is important to think about this as growth of capital. as opposed to the growth in the revenues. Because almost every terrific investment has had some period when the revenues might have gone the other direction. People might have questioned whether it was growthy. Actually, it would be an interesting question. Has NVIDIA ever fallen out of the growth index? I would bet you it has, but I need to go back and validate that. But the point is, it's in the eye of the beholder at any given time. And our approach is sort of look through that and say, look, from where the stock is right now, from what's in front of them, do you think that the stock can grow from here. I will give you one example and be quiet for a second because we're on chips. So it was, I don't know, a couple of years ago, again, I got interested in Intel, right? Intel at the time was very clearly, you know, they were lagging, there were all these challenges. But at the end of the day, one of the things you observed is that if silicon is going to be the oil of the 21st century, a nation having its own supply is crucial. And there is no way that Nvidia, I'm sorry, excuse me, that Intel, is not going to be so important to the U.S. future that we're not going to find a way to make it work, right? And this was before there were signs. But at the time and at the price, there was nothing valued in. It was priced for death. And so the point is you didn't have to sort of see the roadmap in particular. You said the price is so inexpensive and these boundary assets are so important that there will be an intersection of that desirability that will make the stock change in terms of being more coveted and the valuation going up. And that's what I mean by you know, growth of capital.
turns.zh: 而当股价处在这些尖峰的另一侧时，人们又会争论英伟达是否已经不再是一家成长型公司了。所以说实话，对任何一门生意来说，关键在于你所提供的东西的“持续时间”（duration）。而且顺便说一句，我想说的是，没有人拥有永久不变的持续时间。这也是我为什么真心认为，把这件事理解为“资本的增长”很重要，而不是“营收的增长”。因为几乎每一笔出色的投资，都曾经有过某段时间营收可能朝反方向走、人们可能会质疑它还算不算“成长”。其实，这会是个有意思的问题：英伟达有没有曾经从成长指数里被剔除过？我敢打赌有，但我需要回头去验证一下。但重点是，在任何给定的时点，这都取决于观察者的眼光。而我们的方法，某种程度上是穿透这一点，然后说：看，从这只股票现在的价位、从摆在它面前的东西来看，你认为它还能不能从这里继续增长。我给你举一个例子，然后就先安静一会儿，因为我们正好在聊芯片。大概是几年前吧，我又开始对英特尔（Intel）感兴趣，对吧？当时英特尔非常明显地——你知道，它们落后了，有各种各样的挑战。但归根结底，你观察到的一点是：如果说硅（silicon）将成为21世纪的“石油”，那么一个国家拥有自己的供应就至关重要。而英伟达——抱歉，说错了，是英特尔——绝不可能对美国如此重要、而我们却找不到办法让它运转起来，对吧？这还是在出现任何迹象之前。但在当时那个价位上，没有任何好消息被计入股价，它被定价成“死路一条”。所以重点是，你并不一定非要具体看清它的路线图。你说的是：价格便宜到这种地步，而这些“边界性资产”（boundary assets）又如此重要，以至于这种“众人渴望”之间必然会出现一个交汇点，让这只股票发生变化——变得更受追捧，估值随之上升。这就是我所说的“资本的增长”。

turns.en: Okay. Now it's an interesting point. I think a lot of folks, especially in the media, just focus on revenue and earnings growth and that's kind of their definition. So it's definitely another way to look at it. How do you think about, you know, the competitiveness or a competitive advantage of a business? Is that something that you look at and, you know, how a company could protect or strengthen its, you know, ability to generate growth?
turns.zh: 好的。这是个有意思的观点。我想很多人——尤其是媒体——只盯着营收和盈利的增长，那就是他们对“成长”的定义。所以这确实是另一种看待它的方式。那么，你如何看待一门生意的竞争力或竞争优势？这是你会去考察的东西吗？以及一家公司如何保护或强化其产生增长的能力？

turns.en: You're always interested and focused on moats. I would say what is interesting is that over the course of my career, moats have typically gotten smaller. And the market's willingness to recognize a company has a moat, give it credit in its stock price for what that might create, and then anticipate the moat going away, That has gotten shorter and shorter over time. Look, the reason for those, I told you that capital has these one, three, five, eight. The reason for all those is those were supposed to be across full investment cycles, right? Sort of this whole arc. And now what you're seeing is a collapsing of at least in this current market environment, that's the market environment today in the fall of 2026, the journey from out of favor, oh, I think it's going to work, to this is how great it could be, it will work, oh, I'm going to run away from it now, that has gotten so much shorter, right? That is something that's almost dizzying. But the cycle is always the same, right? Is that moat gets competed away, it's the beauty of capitalism, and the question is, is there some enduring way to find additional moats?
turns.zh: 你始终会对“护城河”（moats）感兴趣、并保持关注。我想说的是，有意思的一点是：在我的职业生涯中，护城河通常是越来越窄的。而市场愿意承认一家公司拥有护城河、愿意在股价中为这条护城河可能创造的东西给予溢价、然后再预期这条护城河消失——这一整个过程随着时间推移变得越来越短。你看，之所以有这些——我跟你说过，资本集团有这套一年、三年、五年、八年的考核——所有这些之所以存在，是因为它们本应跨越完整的投资周期，对吧？大致是这一整段弧线。而现在你看到的是——至少在当前这个市场环境下，也就是2026年秋季今天的市场环境——从“不受青睐”，到“哦，我觉得它会成功”，再到“看它可能有多棒、它一定会成功”，最后到“哦，我现在要逃离它了”，这段旅程已经变得短得多，对吧？短到几乎让人头晕目眩。但周期始终是一样的，对吧？护城河被竞争抹平——这正是资本主义的美妙之处——而问题在于，是否存在某种持久的方式去找到新的护城河？

turns.en: And those are the companies that are really extraordinary, by the way. Makes sense. Once you do have conviction in a company, and so I think this might be a little different compared to other managers, you know, with the capital group system, you know, and the different, the PMs, how do you determine position sizing? You know, once you have conviction, it's got, you know, the company is going to enter the fund. How do you figure that out in terms of how are you going to size it? You know, do you talk with the other PMs? No, I don't.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，那些才是真正卓越非凡的公司。有道理。那么，一旦你确实对一家公司有了信念——我想这一点可能和其他管理人不太一样，考虑到资本集团的体系以及不同的投资组合经理——你是如何确定仓位大小的？也就是说，一旦你有了信念，这家公司将要进入基金，你是怎么想清楚该给它多大的仓位的？你会和其他经理交流吗？不，我不会。

turns.en: I mean, well, I always talk to the other PMs, but I don't use it for it to influence my convictions. So, so the, the, This is what can often take a while for people to really get used to with our system. The size that a stock winds up being in the portfolio is really a residual of the number of portfolio managers who are enthusiastic about this. There's not some top-down thing. So I'm going to go back to this metaphor of the farmer's market, what I'm torturing. Imagine We have seven restaurants are going and they're cooking different stuff, right? They have different things, but look, they all love fresh ingredients. They come to this farmer's markets. It's the best stuff in the world, but they're going to go back and they'll have slightly different menus, right? And a couple of may have egg dishes, but they won't all have omelets, right? And so, but there isn't someone that goes, okay, we're going to all coordinate. We're all going to go in and buy potatoes, right? Or we're all going to coordinate. We're all going in and buy peaches. What happens is someone says, you know what? I think people are really in the mood for healthy stuff. And so, There's the healthy restaurant and it's getting those types of ingredients. You've got the other that says, you know, I'm really into breakfast food. And so what winds up populating the aggregate portfolio when you put that all together, right? If you sum all these seven restaurants up and say, oh, how many eggs are in that collection of restaurants or how many fruits? It was a result of those individual decisions, not necessarily some overarching coordination. So with that as sort of the laying out of how things work, then My own personal sizing is based on.
turns.zh: 我是说，嗯，我确实一直会和其他经理交流，但我不会用它来影响我的信念。所以，这……这一点往往是人们要花好一阵子才能真正习惯我们体系的地方。一只股票最终在组合里占多大仓位，实际上是“有多少位投资组合经理对它充满热情”的一个剩余结果（residual）。并不存在某种自上而下的安排。所以我要再回到那个我一直在“折磨”你们的农贸市场的比喻。想象一下，我们有七家餐厅都去采购，它们各自烹饪不同的东西，对吧？它们有不同的菜式，但你看，它们都热爱新鲜食材，都来这个农贸市场，这里是全世界最好的食材。但它们回去后会有略微不同的菜单，对吧？可能有两三家会有蛋类菜肴，但不会家家都做煎蛋卷（omelets），对吧？所以，并没有一个人跳出来说：好，我们大家协调一下，都去买土豆，对吧？或者我们都协调一下，都去买桃子。实际发生的是，某个人说：你知道吗，我觉得大家现在很想吃健康的东西。于是那家“健康餐厅”就去采购那类食材。另一个人说：你知道吗，我特别想做早餐食物。于是，当你把这一切加起来，最终构成整个组合的是什么，对吧？如果你把这七家餐厅加起来，问：这一整群里到底有多少鸡蛋、多少水果？那是这些各自独立决策的结果，而不一定是某种总体的协调。所以，在把运作方式大致铺开之后，我个人的仓位大小则基于——

turns.en: Several things.
turns.zh: ——若干条因素。

turns.en: One, how well I think this idea fits with what my view of what the future is going to look like. Am I getting a great price for it? Do I think there's some durability? Do I think what needs to happen if I'm wrong? For example, some stocks are hard to buy, trade very thin. Look, you're never certain you're 100% right. So I need to make sure that if I'm wrong, can I actually get out and move on and make sure that I correct accordingly? And so those things all go in to create what the size is.
turns.zh: 第一，我认为这个想法与我眼中“未来的样子”契合得有多好。我是不是拿到了一个很棒的价格？我认为它有没有某种持久性？如果我错了，需要发生什么？举个例子，有些股票很难买入、成交非常清淡。看，你永远无法百分之百确定自己是对的。所以我必须确保：万一我错了，我能不能真的出得去、继续前进，并相应地做出纠正。所以，所有这些因素共同决定了仓位的大小。

turns.en: What doesn't go.
turns.zh: 而不会纳入其中的是——

turns.en: In is me saying, oh, the restaurant association, i.e. the index, has this percentage of eggs in there. And so that's what I do. Sometimes it's much bigger. Sometimes it's smaller. To me, it's just about the opportunity.
turns.zh: ——我站出来说：哦，那个“餐厅协会”（restaurant association），也就是指数，里面鸡蛋占了这么个百分比，所以我就照着做。有时候我的仓位比它大得多，有时候更小。对我来说，这只关乎机会本身。

turns.en: Okay. Do you think the multi-manager structure allows individual managers to take more conviction in their best ideas than if they were responsible for the whole portfolio? A thousand percent.
turns.zh: 好的。你认为多经理结构是否让各位经理能够对他们最有把握的想法投入更多信念，超过他们如果要对整个组合负责时所能投入的？百分之百（当然）。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: There are things that I do.
turns.zh: 有些事情我确实会去做。

turns.en: So, if you look right now, I've got three or four positions that are sort of between eight to 12%. Those are, I have occasionally, once or twice in my career, I've gotten something as high as 20% when I had a very high conviction that the runway was strong. There wasn't much, you know, there wasn't much sign that things were abating. But if I were doing the whole thing, I would not do that.
turns.zh: 所以，如果你看现在，我有三四个仓位大概在8%到12%之间。这些是——在我职业生涯中，偶尔有一两次，当我非常有把握、认为跑道很强、几乎没有迹象表明势头会减弱时，我会把某个仓位放到高达20%。但如果要我管理整个组合，我是不会那么做的。

turns.en: I wouldn't do that.
turns.zh: 我不会那么做。

turns.en: The other thing, this system, because there are some other industries I should probably have exposure to, right? I typically only hold between 25 and 35 holdings. A healthy portfolio often will have exposure to some other industries. There's some things that I don't really get, quote unquote, right? I don't get financials, right? So I typically don't invest in those areas. It's not because they're all good ideas. It's just I don't have any edge in terms of when I cast my lens on the world three years out, I don't see any difference.
turns.zh: 另外一点，在这个体系下，因为还有一些别的行业我或许本应有配置，对吧？我通常只持有25到35只股票。一个健康的组合往往会对其他一些行业有配置。但有些东西我真的搞不懂——所谓的“搞懂”，对吧？我搞不懂金融股，对吧？所以我通常不投那些领域。这并不是因为它们都不是好想法，只是当我把目光投向三年后的世界时，我在那里看不到任何优势（edge）、看不到任何区别。

turns.en: It's all fog to me.
turns.zh: 对我来说全是一片迷雾。

turns.en: So one of the things this allows, this system, is I can really focus on just the stuff that I know well or that I think I know well and hold it in the size that I think makes overall sense.
turns.zh: 所以，这个体系让我能做到的一点是：我可以真正专注于那些我很了解、或者我自认为很了解的东西，并以我认为整体上合理的仓位去持有它们。

turns.en: For the portfolio.
turns.zh: 对整个组合而言（合理）。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Um, actually while we're, we're on the topic, I, you know, I think a lot of people are familiar with the multi-manager system, but can you kind of just go a little bit in depth of how it works in practice? You know, other teams, they might kind of share ideas and things, you know, you mentioned having meetings and talking about things. Is there a specific process that goes into how it's all structured? Yep.
turns.zh: 嗯，其实趁着我们在聊这个话题——我想很多人对多经理体系都有所了解，但你能不能再深入讲讲它在实践中是如何运作的？你知道，其他团队他们可能会分享想法之类的，你提到过会开会、讨论各种事情。在如何组织这一切上，有没有一套具体的流程？有的。

turns.en: I think, I think what I often find is when we describe this people, I know how this works and you overlay your existing, um, uh, view. And, but Sierra, let, let me, let me just, hit it straight on. Each manager has, so here, there are seven managers in CDGR, okay? Each one has, and the key to the multiple manager system, right? This system only works if you have seven people who over a long term can outperform And most importantly, they have different ways of going about things. If we were all seven intellectual clones, what's the difference, right? You're all going to sort of go with the same thing. So the hardest thing about this, look, it's hard to find one person that can outperform over a cycle. Having a team of seven really is sort of the gift of a place like Capital. And having people that have worked here for such a long period of time, you've had a chance to test that. So the first thing that sounds easy, but it's actually quite hard, is finding seven outperformers. And then we put them together in a way of You know, how are they different and complementary? That's one of the roles of the PIO to think about, you know, that you have these different complementary skills. And then the other thing that's super important is that we agree on the objective of the fund. We agree on certain rules, like for this one, for example, my market cap's below $ 8 billion. You have to have some level of U.S. sales or exposure, even if it's not necessarily U.S.
turns.zh: 我想，我常常发现，当我们向人们描述这套体系时——我知道它是怎么运作的，而你会把你原有的看法叠加上去。不过，呃……让我直接切入正题吧。每位经理都有——所以这里，CGGR里有七位经理，好吗？每位经理都有（自己的一片组合），而这正是多经理体系的关键，对吧？这套体系只有在这样一种情况下才成立：你有七个人，他们在长期里都能跑赢大盘，而且最重要的是，他们各自处事的方式不同。如果我们七个人都是智力上的克隆体，那又有什么区别呢，对吧？你们都会走向同样的东西。所以这里最难的地方是——你看，要找到一个能在一整个周期里跑赢大盘的人就已经很难了；而要凑齐一个七人团队，真的算是像资本集团这样的地方的一种“天赋”。加上这些人在这里工作了如此长的时间，你就有机会去检验这一点。所以第一件听起来容易、实则相当难的事，就是找到七位能持续跑赢的人。然后我们把他们以一种“他们如何不同、如何互补”的方式组合在一起。这正是首席投资官（PIO）的角色之一：去思考你拥有这些不同的、互补的技能。另一件极其重要的事情是，我们对这只基金的目标达成一致，也对某些规则达成一致。比如说，就这只基金而言，我的选股市值要在80亿美元以下；你必须有一定程度的美国销售或美国业务敞口，即便公司注册地不一定在美国——

turns.en: Domicile.
turns.zh: ——注册地（domicile）。

turns.en: A name like Nintendo or ASML.
turns.zh: 像任天堂（Nintendo）或阿斯麦（ASML）这样的公司，

turns.en: Might be an example.
turns.zh: 可能就是例子。

turns.en: But we agree on the base rules. And then with that agreement, you can go out and construct your portfolio however you'd like. There isn't sort of some, Dave, I think one thing, you think the other. Now we have to debate it. My portfolio slice is what I want it to be. Yours is what yours wants to be. And that last part is super important because one of the challenges is that, at least for me and I find for many of my peers, often our analytical sides have figured out what we want to do or what makes sense. before our verbal sides catch up, right? And so often, you know, there's famous, I have colleagues who say, look, I can't tell you how I know, I just know, right? And what's happened is over decades, you realize, oh yeah, this person, their ability to explain it and persuade just hasn't gotten there yet. So that lets those stocks get into the portfolio, and that's one of the real strengths of it. So at any given time, when you look at these seven slices or the seven restaurants I described, What's on that menu is exactly what that manager wants at that particular time. It's not based on somebody else vetoing, right? The good news is that the quality of the ingredients was sourced by that farmer's market they all shop from, which is our analyst's wisdom and their ideas. So that is what's in aggregate creates this overall menu for people to eat from. In the great food court that is CDGR. Maybe that's what we should do. We should open a food court. Anyway, but that's the... That's the process. That's the capital system. That's how the multiple managers all work together or work together to build a portfolio.
turns.zh: 但我们对这些基本规则达成一致。有了这个共识，你就可以出去、按你喜欢的方式构建你的组合。并不存在那种——戴夫，我是这么想的，你是那么想的，现在我们得辩论一番。我那一片组合就是我想让它成为的样子，你那一片就是你想让它成为的样子。而这最后一点极其重要，因为其中的一个挑战是——至少对我而言，我发现对我很多同行也是如此——我们的分析头脑往往在我们的语言表达跟上来之前，就已经想清楚了我们想做什么、什么才讲得通，对吧？所以经常是这样，你知道，很有名的一点是：我有些同事会说，看，我没法告诉你我是怎么知道的，我就是知道，对吧？而实际发生的是，经过几十年，你会意识到：哦，是的，这个人，他解释和说服的能力还没跟上（他的直觉）。所以这就让那些股票得以进入组合，而这正是这套体系真正的优势之一。因此，在任何给定的时点，当你审视这七片组合、或者说我描述的那七家餐厅时，菜单上是什么，恰恰就是那位经理在那个特定时刻想要的东西。它并不是基于别人来否决，对吧？好消息是，食材的品质是由那个他们都去采购的“农贸市场”来把关的，也就是我们分析师的智慧和他们的想法。所以，正是这一切汇总起来，构成了这份供人们享用的整体菜单——在这个堪称“美食广场”（food court）的CGGR里。也许我们真该去开一个美食广场。总之，但这就是……这就是流程。这就是资本集团的体系。这就是这些多位经理如何协同工作、共同构建一个组合的方式。

turns.en: Okay. No, that's a great explanation. Definitely. You know, I had an idea, but I think that definitely will help our listeners as well kind of understand how it works. If we go back to your, you know, your portfolio specifically, how do you approach risk? Is there kind of a process, you know, you look at in terms of, you know, I mean, with growth, you know, it's, you know, You're making assumptions on the futures. So what do you kind of look at as a risk system?
turns.zh: 好的。不，这是个很棒的解释，绝对如此。我对它原本有些概念，但我认为这也一定能帮助我们的听众理解它是如何运作的。那么，如果我们回到你具体的组合：你是如何看待风险的？有没有一套你会去审视的流程？我是说，对于成长股，你是在对未来做种种假设。所以你把什么当作你的风险控制体系？

turns.en: Yeah, so there's several things. Let's talk about, first of all, there's some embedded guardrails, right? So there are limits we have just as a firm in terms of how much a fund can have in an industry, how big a particular holding can be. There are all those types of limitations that are there as aggregate guardrails, aggregate fencing. As I personally work within that fencing, Look, I am always aware that there are.
turns.zh: 是的，这里有几个方面。我们先说说——首先，有一些内嵌的护栏（guardrails），对吧？也就是我们作为一家公司层面设定的一些限制，比如一只基金在某个行业里最多能配多少、单一持股最大能有多大。所有这些都是作为总体护栏、总体围栏而存在的。当我个人在这个围栏之内工作时——看，我始终清楚，关于未来是——

turns.en: No facts about the future.
turns.zh: ——没有任何确定的事实的。

turns.en: And as much as my conviction is high on something, I am anticipating a future outcome and this future journey. And so I always have to, I always have, okay, there's a chance that I'm not right on this. So make sure that things are either sized appropriately or I realize what I'm looking for if I want to unwind. And that's, to me, an important part of making sure I get, quote unquote, those risks taken care of. There's the risk that you don't really understand the business and the industry. That one, I don't feel very concerned about, knock on wood, because our analysts are so extraordinary and have such long-term context, right? When we tend to miss things, it tends not to be a fundamental thing. It may be, by the way, like the big debate right now. I think the understanding what happens with sort of AI stocks and the fundamentals and what the trajectory is, if things keep doubling, that's all very easy to to sort of parse through. I think the unknowns about how society is going to respond with pushing back on data center construction, possible regulations, what happens if these accidents cause things, those things, those are sort of these great unknowns. But you have to size based on the combination of your knowns, your unknowns, and it I know I'm not being very precise here, but it is a bit of an art form, but it's an art form that I practice within an aggregate structure that says, Alan, you can't have any industry be bigger than 30% of your portfolio, or Alan, you can't have any holding any larger than 40% of your portfolio. Again, that's my own particular slice. The aggregate fund has its own aggregate rules that it won't go over.
turns.zh: 而且，无论我对某件事的信念有多强，我都是在预期一个未来的结果、一段未来的旅程。所以我总是必须——我总是（提醒自己）：好，这件事上我是有可能不对的。所以要确保仓位大小是恰当的，或者确保我心里清楚，如果我想平仓离场，我要找的是什么。对我来说，这是确保我把那些所谓“风险”处理妥当的一个重要部分。还有一种风险，是你其实并不真正理解这门生意和这个行业。这一条我倒不太担心——敲敲木头（图个吉利）——因为我们的分析师极其出色，拥有非常长期的背景积累，对吧？当我们真的看走眼时，往往不是基本面层面的问题。不过话说回来，也可能（是），比如眼下这场大辩论：我理解在AI股票上、在基本面和其轨迹上正在发生什么，如果这些东西持续翻倍，那一切都很容易梳理清楚。我认为真正未知的，是社会将如何回应——比如对数据中心建设的抵制、可能出台的监管，以及万一这些事故发生会引发什么后果，这些才是那些重大的未知数。但你必须基于“已知”与“未知”的组合来决定仓位大小。我知道我这里讲得不是很精确，但它确实有点像是一门艺术，只不过我是在一个总体框架内去实践这门艺术——这个框架会说：艾伦，你任何一个行业都不能超过组合的30%；或者，艾伦，你任何一只持股都不能超过组合的40%。再说一遍，这只是我个人那一片的规则；整只基金还有它自己不会逾越的总体规则。

turns.en: Okay. What about your sell discipline? Is it more of, finding better opportunities or are there times when your original thesis breaks down at some point?
turns.zh: 好的。那你的卖出纪律呢？它更多是关于寻找更好的机会，还是说有时候你最初的投资逻辑会在某个时点崩塌？

turns.en: Story changes lead, right? And the story could change for a couple of reasons. Story could be, look, people didn't appreciate the coil spring. The cycle has happened. People appreciate it. The coil has sprung. Okay, time to sell. It could be, I thought you were going to do X. X didn't happen. It doesn't look like in the foreseeable distance that it's going to happen.
turns.zh: “故事”变了，就离场，对吧？而故事改变可能有几个原因。故事可能是这样：看，人们原本没有领会到那根“压紧的弹簧”；后来周期真的发生了，人们领会到了，弹簧弹了起来。好，是时候卖出了。也可能是：我原以为你会做到X，结果X没有发生，而且在可预见的将来也看不到它会发生。

turns.en: Time to sell.
turns.zh: 是时候卖出了。

turns.en: It could be any number of things, but the short answer is story, change, leave. What is typically not the case, at least for me, I don't tend to use valuation signals as the key to sell because often some of my best ideas, some of the best performing investments have gone much farther than I might have expected. One, because the engine ran longer than I thought or the market's willingness to pay was higher than I thought, but two, But the point is, it tends to not be a valuation signal for me. It's a, the reason that I bought it has changed. Maybe for good reasons, maybe for bad. But reason changes leave.
turns.zh: 它可能是任何数不清的原因，但简短的答案就是：故事变了，就离场。而通常不成立的——至少对我而言——是我一般不会把估值信号当作卖出的关键，因为我最好的一些想法、表现最好的一些投资，往往走得比我预期的远得多。一来是因为那台“引擎”运转的时间比我以为的长，或者市场愿意支付的价格比我以为的高；二来……但重点是，对我来说它往往不是一个估值信号，而是：我当初买入它的理由已经改变了。也许是因为好的原因，也许是因为坏的。但理由变了，就离场。

turns.en: Okay. You know, the fund has a lot of flexibility to invest outside the traditional universe of companies might, you know, people might associate with growth investing. And, you know, you mentioned healthcare a little bit earlier, but are there areas where you're finding opportunities today that might surprise someone only looking at a conventional growth index?
turns.zh: 好的。这只基金有很大的灵活性，可以投资于传统“成长股”范围之外的公司——也就是人们通常会把“成长投资”联想到的那个范围之外。你前面稍微提到了医疗，那么，有没有哪些领域是你今天正在其中发现机会、而可能让一个只看传统成长指数的人感到意外的？

turns.en: Well, you know, so what's interesting to me now is the things, if you go back and look at the things that were in the fund two or three years ago that weren't in the growth index that are now in, right? So a lot of these, so, and that's, by the way, that's one of the things that's very rewarding. But, you know, one of our managers, I told you we have these seven restaurants, but one of the restaurateurs is just a very cautious person when it comes to thinking about the monetary system, what's going to happen with the dollar. And he's in, and so, and so he's always got a growth portfolio that has a lot of tangible things associated with it, right? They can be commodity related. They could be gold streamers, right?
turns.zh: 嗯，你知道，现在让我觉得有意思的是——如果你回头看两三年前这只基金里持有哪些东西、而它们当时不在成长指数里、如今却已经被纳入了，对吧？很多这样的例子。顺便说一句，这也是非常有成就感的事情之一。但是，你知道，我们有位经理——我跟你说过我们有这七家餐厅——其中一位“餐厅老板”在思考货币体系、思考美元将会怎样这些问题时，是一个非常谨慎的人。所以他（也配置了不少），因此他的成长组合里总是有很多与“有形资产”（tangible things）相关的东西，对吧？它们可能是大宗商品相关的，也可能是黄金流融资公司（gold streamers），对吧？

turns.en: They, right.
turns.zh: 它们，对吧。

turns.en: You don't typically think of those, but, but those are really terrific capital appreciation, cap appreciation ideas. At least they have been, uh, when, when, when this person bought them, um, uh, you know, he was buying gold long before the thing got hot, right? So, so that was one of those things that, where the capital appreciation was there and present. One of the things he has been looking at and holds a lot of is performance food group, which is, okay, I mean, it's a sort of a steady Eddie, you know, it's like, but, but he would argue, look, you know, food outside the home is growing at 5%. These guys have compounded areas at 16%. This is a business that that is consolidating. So it's, I guess what I would say is it might be considered quote unquote growth, but it is far from sexy, right? People think people right now equate growth with sexy, right? And often there's a lot of real hidden value in the unsexy, plodding along, steady Eddie, it's going to do well. And so that would be one that, at least when I have one. So the other thing we do, I said, you know, is that we walk around other people's restaurants, right? And I look at, what's that doing in there, right? Because that's the, and so, okay, I see what you're doing. I see where you're doing. It makes sense to me. Okay.
turns.zh: 你通常不会想到那些，但那些其实是非常出色的资本增值（capital appreciation）想法。至少当他买入它们时是这样的——你知道，他在黄金变热之前很久就在买黄金了，对吧？所以那就是那种资本增值实实在在摆在那里的情形。他一直关注、并且大量持有的一只是Performance Food Group（美国食品分销商）。好，我是说，它是那种“稳扎稳打”（steady Eddie）的标的，你知道，它就像……但他会说：看，外出就餐（food outside the home）正以5%的速度增长，而这家公司在某些领域的复合增速达到了16%；这是一门正在整合（consolidating）的生意。所以我想说的是，它也许可以算作所谓的“成长”，但它远谈不上“性感”，对吧？现在人们把“成长”和“性感”划等号，对吧？而往往在那些不性感、慢吞吞、稳扎稳打、注定会做得不错的标的里，藏着大量真正的隐性价值。所以当我也持有这类标的时，那就会是其中之一。另外，我们还会做的一件事——我说过——就是我们也会到别人的餐厅里去逛逛，对吧？然后我会看：那是什么东西，怎么会放在那儿？对吧？因为那就是……于是，好，我明白你在做什么了，我明白你在哪个方向上做，这在我看来讲得通。好。

turns.en: No, it makes a lot of sense. You know, one other question I wanted to just ask about growth index is we all know how, you know, heavily influenced they are now by a relatively small group of very large companies. Do you think that concentration makes the environment more challenging for active growth managers, or do you think it just creates more opportunities elsewhere?
turns.zh: 不，这非常讲得通。我还想再问一个关于成长指数的问题：我们都知道，如今的成长指数在多大程度上被一小撮非常庞大的公司所左右。你认为这种集中度是让主动成长型经理面对的环境更具挑战，还是你认为它只是在他处创造了更多机会？

turns.en: I think it creates more opportunity. I think the question is whether you have a client base who will give you the time to appreciate the opportunity, right? So I can't tell you what and when, but I can soften tell you what, right? And so typically if you look at a portfolio, if you just take the Russell and you look at sort of two or three holdings, making up these gigantic parts of the, by the way, these aren't bad companies, right?
turns.zh: 我认为它创造了更多机会。我觉得问题在于：你是否拥有一个愿意给你时间、让机会得以兑现的客户群体，对吧？所以我没法告诉你“什么时候”，但我基本上能告诉你“是什么”，对吧？因此，通常如果你看一个组合——就以罗素（Russell）指数为例，你看那两三只持股，构成了其中巨大的比重——顺便说一句，这些并不是糟糕的公司，对吧？

turns.en: They're fantastic.
turns.zh: 它们非常出色。

turns.en: But, but should, but should really like, you know, half your money be in four or five, right? And so if I guess, I guess I would say this, if you didn't have time to do your own work, right? And therefore, you just said, look, I need to keep it simple because my day job is doing X. So yeah, if most of my money is in NVIDIA and Apple and whatever the top ones are, okay, got it. You're not going to have great harm. But if you said by the same token, I've got a place that has, in this fund, seven portfolio managers, probably 40 analysts across the spectrum of things. And all they do every day is to go and look for mispriced opportunities where there's a lot of capital appreciation. Yeah, give me some of those, right? Well, there's not room to have those giant positions if you have all this other neat and interesting stuff. So I understand the way we've gotten to this level of concentration, but I think that is exactly the opportunity for us because while all the money sloshed into those, it has left some other things that are quite attractive mispriced.
turns.zh: 但是，但真的应该……你知道，你的一半资金真的应该压在四五只股票上吗，对吧？所以，如果——我想我会这么说——如果你没有时间去做自己的研究，对吧？因此你就说：看，我得保持简单，因为我的本职工作是做X的。那么，是的，如果我大部分的钱都投在英伟达、苹果，以及其他那几只排名靠前的股票上，好，明白，你不会受到什么大的伤害。但同样的道理，如果你说：我手上有一个地方，在这只基金里有七位投资组合经理，跨各个领域大概有40位分析师，而他们每天所做的，就是去寻找那些被错误定价、存在大量资本增值空间的机会。是啊，那给我来一些那样的吧，对吧？嗯，如果你有这么一大堆又棒又有意思的东西，那就没有空间去持有那种巨大的仓位了。所以我理解我们是如何走到今天这种集中度水平的，但我认为，那恰恰是我们的机会所在——因为当所有的钱都涌进那几只股票时，它让另外一些相当有吸引力的东西被错误定价了。

turns.en: Okay. No, I definitely agree with that. We're seeing kind of this huge resurgence in investors loving active at the same time this concentration is happening. And so I think it's kind of a cool storm to watch. And so I have just one more question I wanted to ask before I let you go. You know, when you kind of look at the market today, do you see any disconnect between what investors are focused on in the near term and, you know, growth opportunities that could matter much more over the next, you know, several years? So, okay, I'm going to answer your question. I'm going to tell you why it's hard for me to answer.
turns.zh: 好的。不，我完全同意这一点。我们看到投资者正重新爱上主动管理，出现了巨大的回潮，而与此同时这种集中度也在发生。所以我认为这是一场很酷的、值得关注的“风暴”。那么，在我放你走之前，我还有最后一个问题想问：当你审视今天的市场时，你是否看到投资者近期所关注的东西，与那些在未来几年可能重要得多的成长机会之间，存在某种脱节？好，那我来回答你的问题。我会告诉你为什么这对我来说很难回答。

turns.en: I need to, you know, one of the ways, it's hard for me to keep my perfect pitch in if I'm in a place where there's a bunch of people singing a bunch of other tunes, right?
turns.zh: 我需要——你知道，其中一种方式是：如果我身处一个有一大群人在唱着一堆别的调子的地方，我就很难保持住我的“绝对音准”（perfect pitch），对吧？

turns.en: I'm trying to stay on pitch.
turns.zh: 我在努力保持在调子上。

turns.en: And so I don't spend a lot of time listening to the other singers outside the world, right? I know my singers internally.
turns.zh: 所以我不会花太多时间去听外面世界里其他的“歌手”，对吧？我认识我自己内部的这些“歌手”。

turns.en: I know them. I've calibrated.
turns.zh: 我了解他们，我已经校准过了。

turns.en: We've sung together for decades. I know what that means. But, you know, I don't sit and watch, oh my God, this has gone on TV screaming about this or this lady screaming about that. So one, I'm always a little wary that I don't necessarily understand what other words, what folks are looking for. I guess I would say the following. you know, as we sit here in September, there's a lot of damage being done to physical infrastructure, right? In terms of oil infrastructure, the demands we have on creating power for this magical system, like the physical world moves a lot more slowly than the technological world, right? And so when people say, oh my God, you know, if you think this model is smart, wait till the one, two generations is better. And all you need is sort of, you know, 10 times the power.
